description: We are Welcome Inn STEM Group building PlanetX and SPHEREx project.
summary: Our Team Welcome Inn decided to choose the most difficult of the challenges which was PlanetX and SPHEREx. As we had quite some experience working with NASA APIs we choose to proceed with SPHEREx as a totally new challenge for us to solve and turn it into a public facing tool. We developed a website that showcases the PSX tool that contains a sky map viewer for which we used aladin lite and we used irsa spherex api to fetch spectral images ( fits ) when the user clicks on a certain point on the Sky Map which outputs the RA and DE value, and then user can load the spherex to get a spectral image ( all sky cube ) which can be viewed on 102 different bands. This is important because we were able to accomplish fetching the data as we had come across problems trying to access data through IRSA. In an alternative solution to building a observational tool which required motion vectors which was not working due to irsa's server side problems, ultimately we had choose all sky cube alternative to produce spectral images. Scientists and Students all around the world can now access Project PSX to obtain spectral images of 102 different bands of infrared just by clicking on a certain point on the skymap, making it easier to generate data.
details: PSX lets users generate SPHEREx spectral images(all sky cube) by clicking on a sky map, it can quickly generate spectral images which the user can view on 102 different bands of infrared. We used Visual Studio Code, Miro, Vercel, Render, Github for overall development with ChatGPT/Claude for AI assistance during development in order to maximise our efficiency as we came across many problems. We used NEXT.js, python( numpy, astropy), typescript and CSS to build this project.
